rows: Trees and large limbs were blown down.
Power lines were downed near Normangee. This tornado was a border-crosser and moved from Madison County north into Leon County.
At least three barns and one residence were damaged on CR 977 near CR 210 and also at the intersection of FM 2045 and CR 4025.
Damage was reported along Highway 79 east of Buffalo.
Pea to golfball-size hail was reported by the Buffalo Police Department and relayed by the Centerville Sherriff's office.
Trees were blown down between Buffalo and Jewett.
A tree was blown down and partially blocked Highway 7.
Golfball size hail was reported near Oakwood.
Penny size hail fell in Centerville.
A spotter estimated a 60 MPH wind gust in Buffalo.
A 65 MPH wind gust was estimated in Centerville.
Quarter size hail fell 2 miles south of Leona.
Golfball size hail fell 4 miles south of the town of Buffalo.
Tree limbs that were 1-2 in diameter were down on the south side of Marquez.
Several large tree limbs and at least one large tree was blown down in Normangee.
Half Dollar size hail was reported 4 miles west of Leona.
Nickel size hail fell in the town of Flo.
A couple of trees were knocked down in Jewett.
Penny size hail fell in Hilltop Lake.
Sixty MPH winds were estimated in Jewett.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred approximately 1 mile east of Oakwood. This tornado had a path length of approximately 1 mile and an estimated width of 100 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75 mph.
Large tree limbs were knocked off trees with estimated 70 MPH winds associated with the rear flank downdraft of the thunderstorm.
Golfball size hail fell at the intersection of Farm-to-Market Road 39 and Highway 7.
Quarter sized hail fell on Highway 79, approximately halfway between Jewett and Buffalo.
Dime sized hail was reported by the COOP Observer in Centerville.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked down a few tree limbs and also destroyed 2 sheds. This damage occurred near FM 1618 and Private Road 3365; just west of Interstate 45.
Penny sized hail was reported between Buffalo and Donie.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees on Blackjack Street in Jewett.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees near CR 317 and CR 314 in the Jewett area.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees in the Hilltop Lakes area.
Quarter sized hail was reported in the Hilltop Lakes development in southwest Leon County.
Golf ball sized hail was reported in the Hilltop Lakes development in southwest Leon County.
Sixty-five MPH winds were estimated in Centerville. The strong winds brought down power lines, caused minor roof damage, and damaged the side of one building.
Damaging thunderstorm winds knocked down and damaged large pine trees 3 miles south of Centerville. 65 mph winds had been estimated in Centerville.
Three 12 trees were knocked down along Highway 164 about half a mile west of I-45.
Penny sized hail was reported at Highway 79 and FM 832 between Buffalo and Oakwood.
Hail to the size of golf balls was reported in Marquez.
Dime to nickel sized hail was reported in Marquez.
A trained spotter reported a small barn being blown across State Hwy 75 near Garland Road, about 5 miles south-southeast of Buffalo, TX.
A trained spotter reported 2 to 4 inch diameter tree limbs blown down in the city of Marquez, TX.
An amateur radio operator reported that a barn and a shop were destroyed by thunderstorm winds on County Road 431.
Leon County Sheriff's Department reported trees down on Highway 79.
Leon County Sheriff's Department reported that a barn ended up in the middle of Highway 7 near Marquez.
Leon County Sheriff's Department reported approximately 30 trees knocked down along CR 386.
Leon County Sheriff's Department reported that the roofs of 6 chicken houses were blown off and other debris was scattered about in the area.
Amateur radio reported that several 40 plus feet tall pine trees were blown over, and the front wall of a double-wide wide was torn from the structure off County Road 431.
Leon County Sheriff's Department reported that as 18 wheeler hit a downed tree near the town of Normangee.
One inch hail was reported in Leona.
Golf ball size hail fell just northeast of Buffalo.
Trained spotter reported quarter size hail 3 miles west of Marquez.
A trained spotter reported golf ball size hail 5 miles southwest of Oakwood.
Emergency Manager reported a sign and one power line down between Buffalo and Centerville.
A public report indicated trees down off CR 458 and CR 459.
A public report indicated quarter-sized hail at a gas station along Interstate 45 approximately 4 miles south of the city of Leona, TX.
A public report indicated golf ball to hen-egg size hail in the city of Marquez, TX.
A trained spotter reported half-dollar size hail in the city of Buffalo, TX.

This tornado is a continuation from Milam and Robertson counties. After entering from eastern Robertson County, the tornado dissipated in extreme western Leon County, 4 miles south-southwest of Marquez. Only tree damage was observed along the path in Leon County.

A trained spotter reported quarter size hail approximately 5 miles west of the city of Centerville, TX.
Emergency management reported 20 to 40 trees down on Highway 79 in the city of Marquez, TX.

A trained spotter reported damage to a metal building on FM 39 south of Highway 7.
An MPING report indicated trees snapped or uprooted approximately 12 miles southeast of Oakwood, TX.
A swath of thunderstorm wind damage was found from Hwy 7 and FM 1511 to FMs 148 and 149. Large trees were damaged or uprooted, an airplane hangar was damaged, and a few homes sustained roof damage.
Emergency management reported golf ball sized hail approximately 12 miles south-southeast of the city of Oakwood.
Emergency management reported several small trees being blown down approximately 12 miles south-southeast of the city of Coolidge, TX.
Emergency management reported a 10x10 portable shed blown over, along with minor damage to a roof and tree limbs, approximately 11 miles south-southeast of the city of Coolidge, TX.
A public report indicated dime sized hail about 4 miles west southwest of Leona, TX.
Broadcast media reported quarter sized hail about a mile east of Leona, TX.
A photograph posted on social media indicated golf ball sized hail in Leona, TX.
Damage was reported in Centerville, including multiple downed power lines and trees. One power pole and one tree was down on top of a house. A tree also fell on a car.
Several broken trees and large tree limbs were observed along Highway 7 near County Road 203 east of Centerville.
Quarter sized hail was reported in eastern Leon County near CR 112.

A parked 18-wheeler with a box trailer was flipped, and a nearby utility pole was bent.
Broadcast media reported that a tractor barn made of sheet metal was destroyed in Buffalo, TX.
Trained spotter reported quarter sized hail 2 miles south of Jewett via amateur radio.
Amateur radio reported multiple trees down on Highways 7, 79, and 39 in the vicinity of Jewett, Marquez, and Normangee.

One fallen tree fell on a home on Highway 7 east of Marquez causing damage to the roof, garage, and windows. In the same area, a wood and metal roof was torn off a barn, trees were split, a 5th wheel was overturned, and electric equipment on a tower was torn off.
Amateur radio operator reported quarter hail 5 miles west of Centerville.
Emergency manager reported trees and power lines blown down along Hwy 7 between FM 542 and the Trinity River, and a hay barn was blown down on the north side of Hwy 7 near Trinity River.
A storm chaser reported 70 mph winds and power outages in Leona on FM 977. Reports on Facebook also indicated several trees were down along Highway 75 in Leona.
Facebook photos showed two large barns with roofs blown off and one shop with overhead doors partially blown in on FM 1469 near PR 3550 north of Marquez.

On the south end of Jewett, outside the tornado track, large tree limbs were broken and some trees were uprooted.
